text:
maria_csops: Heads up — we saw a ~22% jump in accounts flagged as ‘Healthy’ in yesterday’s snapshot. Looks correlated with a batch import from the legacy onboarding tool that created duplicate contact records. Playbooks are happily firing because activity appears across multiple contact rows for the same account. :eyes:

eva_data: I pulled a quick join of contacts -> accounts. The duplicates have slight variations (email+alias, phone formatting). Query I used:```sql
SELECT account_id, count(*) AS contact_count, array_agg(distinct email)
FROM crm_contacts
WHERE created_at > '2025-12-01'
GROUP BY account_id
HAVING count(*) > 1
ORDER BY contact_count DESC
LIMIT 200;
```
Notably ~40% are from importer job `legacy-sync-v2` and have empty `canonical_id` field.

maria_csops: Ok — so playbooks see multiple contacts with recent activity and mark account engaged. We need a pre-playbook canonicalization step (non-destructive) to tag likely-duplicates and run playbooks only on canonical=true rows during dry-run. Would prefer this be reversible for a few days.

aj_eng: Agree with pre-step. Two implementation options: 1) ETL side: create a daily preprocessor that sets `canonical_candidate` and `canonical_score`, writes to a staging column, then playbook service reads that staging column; 2) Playbook side: add a filter phase that collapses contacts into canonical clusters before rule evaluation. Option 1 is faster to roll back.

aj_eng: Quick pseudo for preprocessor (batch):```python
# run canonicalizer
for account in accounts_with_dups:
  candidates = fetch_contacts(account)
  canonical = pick_best(candidates)
  update_contacts(canonical_id=canonical.id, staged_canonical=true)
```
We can ship the preprocessor as a daily cron under /data-pipelines and expose a feature flag.

priya_product: Feature flag + staged dry-run is a must. Product asks: can we sample 5% of accounts first and compare playbook outcomes vs baseline before full rollout? Also want a small UX note for CSMs explaining that duplicates will be merged for playbooks only (not actual merge).

maria_csops: Yes to 5% sample. Also want to add a healthscore regressions check — if overall account renewal-risk score drops >3% after canonicalization for the sample, pause and audit.

playbook-bot: Automated report: playbook-run 2026-01-21 03:00 — accounts evaluated: 12,432 — flagged changes: 1,212 — duplicates-tagged: 1,004. /details -> https://internal-reports/redwood/playbooks/2026-01-21

tom_sre: Heads-up on implementation constraints: current webhook queue for CRM updates peaks during import windows. If the preprocessor writes N updates per contact we could overwhelm the ingest pipeline. Recommend batching writes and using the bulk update endpoint (/api/v1/contacts/bulk) with backoff; also add a short windowed rate-limit in the pipeline.

aj_eng: Good call. We'll implement bulk writes and exponential backoff. Also will make the preprocessor write to a staging namespace first (crm_contacts_staging) to avoid triggering hooks in prod until we flip the feature flag.

maria_csops: Action items: 1) aj_eng to prototype preprocessor + staging write (ETA 2 days) 2) eva_data to generate 5% sample list and baseline metrics (ETA 24h) 3) priya_product to draft CSM note + opt-in for sampling cohort (ETA 48h) 4) tom_sre to validate bulk endpoint capacity and set rate limits (ETA 48h). I'll coordinate dry-run next Monday and post results here. :thumbsup:

priya_product: I'll also add a small FAQ blurb for the CSM app about 'playbook-only canonicalization' so they don't see data as permanently merged.

maria_csops: If anyone wants to pair on the canonical scoring rules I can share the initial matching heuristic (email cleaned + normalized phone + name-similarity threshold). Happy to hop on a quick call.

aj_eng: I'll take pairing. tagging as owner for the preprocessor PR.

maria_csops: Thanks team — will update after the sample run.
